chapter.name: Preamble
chapter.blurb: Meaning of the Preamble's key words, forms of democracy, justice-liberty-equality-fraternity, its amendment and the cases on its status.

scope_in.item: Preamble: origin, descriptions, key words (sovereign, socialist, secular, democratic, republic), direct and indirect democracy, secularism comparison
Justice, liberty, equality (Articles 14-18, 325-326, 39), fraternity, union of trinity
Preamble cases, amendment by the 42nd Amendment, significance table

scope_out.item: Western-versus-Indian secularism table rows on historical roots, public display of religion and State interference
scope_out.reason: interpretive generalisations not supported by Laxmikanth or settled law

scope_out.item: Golak Nath attribution of the 'soul of the Constitution'
scope_out.reason: attribution doubtful; Laxmikanth credits the phrase to Hidayatullah

concepts.name: Key words of the Preamble: sovereign, socialist, secular, democratic, republic, justice, liberty
concepts.description: Meaning of We the People, sovereign, socialist, secular (Indian versus Western), democratic with the devices of direct democracy, indirect democracy, republic, and the dimensions of justice and liberty.
concepts.idea: Each key word of the Preamble has a precise meaning and a typical confusion: democratic socialism is not State socialism, positive secularism is not strict separation, and each device of direct democracy does a different job.
concepts.rule: The Preamble is called the identity card of the Constitution and draws on the Objectives Resolution. Sovereign means supreme authority over internal and external policy; Socialist (1976) means democratic socialism with a mixed economy; Secular (1976) means equal respect and no State religion, in the positive Indian sense unlike the strict separation of the West. Democratic covers political and social democracy: direct democracy (Switzerland) uses initiative, recall, referendum and plebiscite, while indirect democracy is parliamentary or presidential. A republic has an elected, not hereditary, head of State. Justice is social, economic and political; distributive justice is the social-economic combination; liberty is absence of unreasonable restraints.
concepts.example: A State puts a proposed law to a direct vote of the electorate: that is a referendum, a device of direct democracy.

questions.q: A jurist's description of the Preamble as the 'identity card of the Constitution' is among the most quoted in Indian polity. Which one of the following is credited with that description?
questions.e: The 'identity card of the Constitution' phrase is N.A. Palkhivala's. Munshi called the Preamble the 'horoscope of our sovereign democratic republic', Hidayatullah the 'soul' of the Constitution, and Iyer said it expresses what the founders had long dreamt.
w: Munshi's own phrase for the Preamble was 'horoscope of our sovereign democratic republic'.
Hidayatullah is quoted for 'the soul of our Constitution', not for the identity-card phrase.
Alladi Krishnaswami Iyer said the Preamble expresses what the framers had thought and dreamt, not that it is an identity card.

questions.q: A State nationalises a few strategic sectors but allows private enterprise to operate alongside the public sector in other fields. Which one of the following best describes the 'socialist' ideal of the Preamble that this policy reflects?
questions.a: Democratic socialism resting on a mixed economy of public and private sectors
o: Democratic socialism resting on a mixed economy of public and private sectors
State socialism that nationalises all means of production and distribution
Laissez-faire capitalism that leaves the reduction of inequality to the market
Communism in which private property is abolished and production is community-owned
questions.e: The Indian brand is democratic socialism with a mixed economy in which public and private sectors co-exist, not State ownership of all means of production. The term signals commitment to social and economic justice and to preventing concentration of wealth.
w: State (communistic) socialism nationalises everything and abolishes private property, which the Indian model does not do.
The Preamble's socialism aims at reducing inequality; laissez-faire leaves that to the market and so is not the ideal.
Abolition of private property with community ownership is the communistic model, which is distinct from democratic socialism.

questions.q: A proposed law, instead of being finally decided by the legislature, is referred to the electorate, whose direct vote settles whether it is adopted. Which device of direct democracy is this?
questions.e: A referendum refers a proposed law (or constitutional amendment) to the voters, who approve or reject it. Initiative lets citizens propose a bill, recall removes a representative, and a plebiscite obtains opinion on a major issue, generally a territorial one.
w: Initiative means citizens draft a proposal and submit it, rather than voting on the legislature's proposal.
Recall removes an elected representative before the term ends and does not decide a law.
A plebiscite takes the people's opinion on a major political issue, often territorial, rather than approving a specific proposed law.

questions.q: Which one of the following countries is correctly described, in the standard classification of forms of government, as having an executive accountable to the legislature together with a hereditary head of State?
questions.e: Parliamentary systems (India, UK) make the executive accountable to Parliament, and the UK is a monarchy with a hereditary ruler. India is a parliamentary republic with an elected President; the USA has a presidential system; Switzerland is the example of direct democracy.
w: India is parliamentary but a republic: the President is elected, not hereditary.
The USA is presidential and its head of State is elected, so neither condition holds.
Switzerland is cited as the example of direct democracy and has no hereditary head of State.

questions.q: Which one of the following sets lists the ideals of the Preamble that are traced to the French Revolution (1789-1799)?
questions.e: The ideals of liberty, equality and fraternity are traditionally traced to the French Revolution (1789-1799); the ideal of justice is traced to the Russian Revolution (1917), so every set containing 'justice' is wrong.
w: This set includes justice, which is traced to the Russian Revolution of 1917.
This set includes justice, a Russian Revolution ideal, and omits liberty.
This set includes justice, a Russian Revolution ideal, and omits equality.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Preamble's character and origin:

1. It is described as the identity card of the Constitution and as a key to the minds of its framers.
2. The Objectives Resolution, from which the Preamble draws its origin, was moved by Nehru and adopted by the Constituent Assembly on the same day, 13 December 1946.
3. The Preamble is often described as the summary and philosophy of the Constitution.
4. The Preamble was taken over unchanged from the Objectives Resolution and has never been altered since.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: the Preamble is described as the identity card of the Constitution and a key to the minds of its framers. Statement 2 is incorrect: the Objectives Resolution was moved on 13 December 1946 and adopted on 22 January 1947. Statement 3 is correct: the Preamble is described as the summary or essence of the Constitution. Statement 4 is incorrect: it was amended once, in 1976 by the 42nd Amendment.
w: '1 and 2 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect, and leaves out statement 3, which is correct.
'3 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect, and leaves out statement 1, which is correct.
'1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about sovereignty and the opening words of the Preamble:

1. Sovereignty in the Preamble covers India's external policy, while its internal law-making lies outside the concept.
2. The opening words 'We, the People of India' place ultimate sovereign power in the citizens rather than in any external authority or ruler.
3. A sovereign State is free to make its own laws and conduct its internal and external policy without outside interference.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: sovereignty means supreme authority over internal and external policy alike. Statement 2 is correct: also(source of authority). Statement 3 is correct: also.
w: '1 and 3 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct:
'1 and 2 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct:
'2 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct:

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the word 'Socialist' in the Preamble:

1. The word signals a commitment to social and economic justice and to preventing wealth from concentrating in a few hands.
2. The word was inserted into the Preamble by the 44th Amendment Act, 1978.
3. The Indian brand denotes democratic socialism with a mixed economy, not State ownership of all means of production.
4. Socialism in its general sense refers to a system in which the means of production are owned or regulated by the community or the State to reduce inequality.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: The word signals a commitment to social and economic justice and to preventing wealth from concentrating in a few hands. Statement 2 is incorrect: it was added by the 42nd Amendment, 1976. Statement 3 is correct: The Indian brand denotes democratic socialism with a mixed economy, not State ownership of all means of production. Statement 4 is correct: Socialism in its general sense refers to a system in which the means of production are owned or regulated by the community or the State to reduce inequality.
w: '1, 2 and 4 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct:
'2, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct:
'1 and 3 only' leaves out statement 4, which is correct:

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the word 'Secular' in the Preamble:

1. The word 'Secular' formed part of the Preamble as adopted on 26 November 1949 and was left untouched by the 42nd Amendment.
2. In the Indian sense, secular means equal respect and treatment of all religions by the State, which has no State religion of its own.
3. The Indian model is described as positive secularism, in which all religions have the same status and support from the State.
4. The Supreme Court observed in 1974 that the Constitution-makers intended a secular State, which is why Articles 25 to 28 on freedom of religion were included.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: 'Secular' was added to the Preamble by the 42nd Amendment, 1976. Statement 2 is correct: in the Indian sense, secular means equal respect and treatment of all religions by the State, which has no State religion of its own. Statement 3 is correct: Indian secularism is a positive concept, in which all religions have the same status and support from the State. Statement 4 is correct: the Court (1974) saw Articles 25 to 28 as reflecting the framers' intent of a secular State, long before the 1976 insertion.
w: '1, 2 and 4 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect, and leaves out statement 3, which is correct.
'1, 2, 3 and 4' includes statement 1, which is incorrect.
'3 and 4 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about secularism in India:

1. Indian secularism rests on equal respect for all religions, whereas the Western model stands for strict separation of Church and State.
2. The Supreme Court observed in 1974 that, although the words 'secular state' were not expressly used in the Constitution as framed, its makers wanted such a State, which is why Articles 25 to 28 on freedom of religion were included.
3. Unlike a model of strict separation, the Indian State can take part in some religious activities, such as funding religious institutions.
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Indian secularism rests on equal respect for all religions, whereas the Western model stands for strict separation of Church and State. Statement 2 is correct:(Supreme Court, 1974). Statement 3 is correct: the Indian State is not required to keep away from religion altogether, unlike the strict-separation model. All three are correct.
w: '2 and 3 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct:
'1 and 2 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct:
'1 and 3 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct:

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about democracy under the Preamble:

1. Democracy in India gives citizens equal political rights and the power to elect leaders, but holding elected leaders accountable lies outside the idea.
2. Popular sovereignty, on which Indian democracy rests, means that all authority flows from Parliament.
3. The word 'democratic' in the Preamble covers political democracy as well as social democracy.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: accountability of elected leaders is commonly listed as part of Indian democracy. Statement 2 is incorrect: authority flows from 'We, the People', not from Parliament. Statement 3 is correct: the Preamble's 'democratic' covers political democracy and also social and economic democracy.
w: '1 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect, and leaves out statement 3, which is correct.
'1 and 3 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect.
'2 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect, and leaves out statement 3, which is correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the devices of direct democracy:

1. Under the initiative, citizens draft a proposal and submit it for a legislative or public vote.
2. Under the recall, people remove an elected representative before the term ends.
3. A plebiscite is a direct vote on a major political issue, often a territorial or constitutional one.
4. Initiative, recall and referendum are three devices of direct democracy, and the veto is the fourth.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: under the initiative, people propose a bill to the legislature. Statement 2 is correct: under the recall, people remove an elected representative before the term ends. Statement 3 is correct: a plebiscite is a vote on a major issue, generally used to settle territorial disputes. Statement 4 is incorrect: the fourth device is the plebiscite, not the veto.
w: '1, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect, and leaves out statement 2, which is correct.
'1 and 3 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct.
'1 and 2 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about indirect democracy:

1. In indirect democracy citizens elect representatives who decide for them, and it is the most widely adopted form in modern States.
2. Representative democracy in the indirect form is either parliamentary or presidential.
3. In the presidential system, as in the USA, the executive is accountable to the legislature for its continuance in office.
4. Switzerland is the standard example of indirect democracy.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: indirect or representative democracy has citizens elect representatives who decide for them. Statement 2 is correct: representative democracy is either parliamentary or presidential. Statement 3 is incorrect: that describes the parliamentary system (India, UK); in the presidential system the President is both Head of State and Government and is not accountable to the legislature for continuance in office. Statement 4 is incorrect: Switzerland is the standard example of direct democracy.
w: '1 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect, and leaves out statement 2, which is correct.
'2 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect, and leaves out statement 1, which is correct.
'2 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about justice and liberty in the Preamble:

1. Political justice means the reduction of inequalities in wealth, income and property.
2. Social justice aims at the upliftment of SCs, STs and OBCs but not of women.
3. Justice means fair, equal and balanced treatment of every individual, and liberty means absence of unreasonable restraints on action, supporting personal autonomy and the growth of personality.
4. Social justice demands equal treatment irrespective of caste, religion, race, gender or colour and the removal of social privileges.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: that is economic justice; political justice is equal political rights, universal participation and equal opportunity to hold office. Statement 2 is incorrect: women are included among those whose conditions are to be improved. Statement 3 is correct: Justice means fair, equal and balanced treatment of every individual, and liberty means absence of unreasonable restraints on action, supporting personal autonomy and the growth of personality. Statement 4 is correct: Social justice demands equal treatment irrespective of caste, religion, race, gender or colour and the removal of social privileges.
w: '1 and 3 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct:
'1 and 4 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct:
'2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct:

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about justice in the Preamble:

1. Economic justice seeks to reduce inequalities in wealth, income and property and to give fair opportunity of livelihood.
2. Distributive justice is the combination of economic justice and political justice.
3. The Preamble's justice is secured by provisions found in both the Fundamental Rights and the Directive Principles.
4. Political justice includes universal participation in governance and an equal opportunity to hold public office.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Economic justice seeks to reduce inequalities in wealth, income and property and to give fair opportunity of livelihood. Statement 2 is incorrect: distributive justice is the combination of social justice and economic justice, not of economic and political justice. Statement 3 is correct: justice is secured through Fundamental Rights and Directive Principles. Statement 4 is correct:(equal access to political offices). So only three of the statements are correct.
w: 'Only two' miscounts: the correct statement(s) are 1, 3, 4.
'All four' miscounts: the correct statement(s) are 1, 3, 4.
'Only one' miscounts: the correct statement(s) are 1, 3, 4.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about equality and the sources of the Preamble's ideals:

1. Equality means absence of special privileges and equal opportunity for all without discrimination.
2. The Preamble secures equality of status and opportunity in four dimensions: civic, social, political and economic.
3. The ideals of liberty, equality and fraternity are inspired by the Russian Revolution of 1917.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Equality means absence of special privileges and equal opportunity for all without discrimination. Statement 2 is incorrect: it names three dimensions, civic, political and economic. Statement 3 is incorrect: they are inspired by the French Revolution, 1789-1799; the Russian Revolution is the source of justice. So only one of the statements is correct.
w: 'None' miscounts: the correct statement(s) are 1.
'Only two' miscounts: the correct statement(s) are 1.
'All three' miscounts: the correct statement(s) are 1.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the republic in the Preamble:

1. A republic is a form of government in which the head of State is elected, not hereditary, directly or indirectly for a fixed term.
2. The President, India's elected head of State, is chosen indirectly for a fixed term of five years.
3. In a republic, political sovereignty vests in a single individual such as a king.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: A republic is a form of government in which the head of State is elected, not hereditary, directly or indirectly for a fixed term. Statement 2 is correct: The President, India's elected head of State, is chosen indirectly for a fixed term of five years. Statement 3 is incorrect: a republic vests political sovereignty in the people, not in a single individual. So only two of the statements is correct.
w: 'Only one' miscounts: the correct statement(s) are 1, 2.
'None' miscounts: the correct statement(s) are 1, 2.
'All three' miscounts: the correct statement(s) are 1, 2.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: The Indian Constitution embodies the positive concept of secularism, in which all religions have the same status and support from the State.
Statement-II: The Indian model of secularism requires the strict separation of Church and State.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
o: Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct: the Indian Constitution embodies a positive concept of secularism in which all religions have the same status and support from the State. Statement-II is incorrect: strict separation of Church and State is the Western model, whereas Indian secularism means equal respect for all religions.
w: Rejected: 'Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I' does not match the verdict on the two statements: I correct, II incorrect.
Rejected: 'Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I' does not match the verdict on the two statements: I correct, II incorrect.
Rejected: 'Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct' does not match the verdict on the two statements: I correct, II incorrect.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: The United Kingdom, although it has a parliamentary executive, is not a republic.
Statement-II: The head of State of the United Kingdom holds a hereditary position.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct: a republic needs an elected head of State, and the UK is cited as a monarchy. Statement-II is correct: the UK is the example of a monarchy with a hereditary ruler, which is exactly why it is not a republic. Statement-II gives the reason for Statement-I.
w: Rejected: 'Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I' does not match the verdict on the two statements: both are correct, and II does explain I.
Rejected: 'Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect' does not match the verdict on the two statements: both are correct, and II does explain I.
Rejected: 'Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct' does not match the verdict on the two statements: both are correct, and II does explain I.

questions.q:
Match the situation in List-I with the device of direct democracy it illustrates in List-II.

List-I
A. Voters of a constituency collect signatures to remove their representative before the term ends
B. Citizens draft a bill and send it to the legislature for enactment
C. A proposed constitutional amendment is put to the electorate to accept or reject
D. The inhabitants of a disputed territory vote on which State they wish to join

List-II
1. Initiative
2. Recall
3. Referendum
4. Plebiscite
questions.e: Recall removes a representative before the term ends, initiative proposes a bill, referendum approves or rejects a measure such as a constitutional amendment, and plebiscite settles a major, often territorial, issue.
w: Recall and initiative are interchanged: removal before term is recall.
Referendum and plebiscite are interchanged: the territorial vote is a plebiscite.
Recall and referendum are interchanged: removal is recall, and approving an amendment is a referendum.

concepts.name: Equality, fraternity, the trinity, amendment and cases on the Preamble
concepts.description: Articles securing civic, political and economic equality, fraternity and its two assurances, Ambedkar's union of trinity, the 42nd Amendment and the cases on the Preamble.
concepts.idea: Equality rests on Articles 14-18, 325-326 and 39; the Preamble is part of the Constitution and amendable only within the basic structure, as shown by the Berubari-Kesavananda-LIC line of cases.
concepts.rule: Civic equality rests on Articles 14 to 18, political equality on Articles 325 and 326 and economic equality on Article 39, a Directive Principle. Fraternity must assure the dignity of the individual and the unity and integrity of the Nation. Ambedkar treated liberty, equality and fraternity as a union of trinity. Berubari (1960) held the Preamble not part of the Constitution, Kesavananda Bharati (1973) held it a part, amendable under Article 368 but not in its basic features, and the LIC case (1995) reaffirmed it as an integral part that is not directly enforceable. It has been amended once, by the 42nd Amendment (1976), which added Socialist, Secular and Integrity.
concepts.example: A caste is left out of the electoral rolls: Article 325 is violated.

questions.q: A State declares citizens of a particular caste ineligible for inclusion in the electoral rolls. Which provision, listed under political equality in the Preamble's scheme, does this most directly violate?
questions.e: Article 325 says nobody can be declared ineligible for inclusion in the electoral rolls on grounds of religion, race, caste or sex. Article 326 provides adult suffrage for Lok Sabha and State Assembly elections, Article 16 concerns public employment and Article 17 untouchability.
w: Article 326 lays down adult suffrage for elections to the Lok Sabha and State Assemblies; the exclusion from rolls is addressed by Article 325.
Article 16 gives equal opportunity in public employment, not in electoral rolls.
Article 17 abolishes untouchability and does not deal with electoral rolls.

questions.q: Of the three dimensions of equality named in the Preamble's scheme, which one rests on a Directive Principle of State Policy rather than on Fundamental Rights or election provisions?
o: None of them, since all three dimensions rest on Fundamental Rights
questions.e: Economic equality rests on Article 39, a Directive Principle that provides for equal pay for equal work and adequate means of livelihood; civic equality rests on Articles 14 to 18 and political equality on Articles 325 and 326.
w: Civic equality is secured by Articles 14 to 18 in the Fundamental Rights chapter.
Political equality is secured by Articles 325 and 326 on electoral rolls and adult suffrage.
Economic equality rests on Article 39, a Directive Principle, so it is wrong to say that all three rest on Fundamental Rights.

questions.q: The Preamble as originally adopted spoke of the 'Unity of the Nation'. Which one of the following gives its present wording and the amendment responsible?
questions.a: 'Unity and Integrity of the Nation', 42nd Amendment Act, 1976
o: 'Unity and Integrity of the Nation', 42nd Amendment Act, 1976
'Unity and Integrity of the Nation', 44th Amendment Act, 1978
'Unity and Sovereignty of the Nation', 42nd Amendment Act, 1976
'Unity and Integrity of the Nation', 7th Amendment Act, 1956
questions.e: The 42nd Amendment (1976) changed 'Unity of the Nation' to 'Unity and Integrity of the Nation', stressing territorial and psychological unity.
w: The 44th Amendment (1978) did not touch the Preamble; the Preamble has been amended only once.
'Sovereignty' is not the word added; the added word is Integrity.
The 7th Amendment (1956) did not amend the Preamble.

questions.q: A State begins to confer inheritable titles of nobility on certain families. Which provision in the group of articles securing civic equality does this most directly offend?
questions.e: Article 18 abolishes titles so that no privileged class is created. Article 15 bars discrimination on named grounds, Article 16 concerns public employment and Article 17 abolishes untouchability.
w: Article 15 prohibits discrimination on grounds such as religion, race, caste, sex and place of birth, not conferment of titles.
Article 16 deals with equality of opportunity in public employment.
Article 17 abolishes untouchability.

questions.q: Which one of the following best represents Dr B.R. Ambedkar's description of fraternity?
questions.a: A sense of common brotherhood among all Indians
o: A sense of common brotherhood among all Indians
The absence of unreasonable restraints on individual action
Equal respect and equal treatment of all religions by the State
A direction to secure equal pay for equal work
questions.e: Ambedkar described fraternity as the sentiment of shared brotherhood among all Indians, reflecting emotional unity, mutual respect and belonging. Freedom from restraints is liberty, equal treatment of religions is secularism, and equal pay is Article 39.
w: Absence of unreasonable restraints defines liberty.
Equal respect for all religions is the Indian meaning of secular.
Equal pay for equal work is in Article 39, a Directive Principle.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about civic equality:

1. Civic equality is secured through Articles 14 to 18.
2. Article 14 keeps the State from denying any person equality before the law or the equal protection of the laws.
3. Article 15 forbids the State from discriminating against citizens on the ground of religion, race, caste, sex or place of birth.
4. Article 16 is the provision on equal opportunity for those seeking public jobs.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Civic equality is secured through Articles 14 to 18. Statement 2 is correct: Article 14. Statement 3 is correct: this is Article 15 (Article 17 abolishes untouchability). Statement 4 is correct. All four are correct.
w: '1, 2 and 4 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct:
'1, 2 and 3 only' leaves out statement 4, which is correct:
'1, 3 and 4 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct:

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Articles 15, 17 and 18:

1. Article 17 abolishes untouchability.
2. Article 15 bars the State from discriminating on the basis of religion, race, caste, sex, descent or place of birth.
3. Article 18 abolishes titles so as to prevent the creation of privileged classes.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Article 17 abolishes untouchability. Statement 2 is incorrect: descent is not among the grounds listed for Article 15: religion, race, caste, sex and place of birth. Statement 3 is correct: Article 18 abolishes titles so as to prevent the creation of privileged classes.
w: '1 and 2 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct:
'1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect:
'2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct:

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about political equality:

1. Political equality rests on Articles 325 and 326.
2. Article 325 forbids keeping a citizen off the electoral rolls on the basis of religion, race, caste or sex.
3. Article 326 provides adult franchise for elections to the Rajya Sabha and the State Legislative Councils.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Political equality rests on Articles 325 and 326. Statement 2 is correct: Article 325 forbids keeping a citizen off the electoral rolls on the basis of religion, race, caste or sex. Statement 3 is incorrect: Article 326 applies to elections to the Lok Sabha and the State Assemblies.
w: '1 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct:
'2 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct:
'2 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct:

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about economic equality:

1. Economic equality rests on Article 51-A, a Fundamental Duty.
2. Article 39 is a Fundamental Right enforceable by the courts.
3. Article 39 directs the State to secure equal pay for equal work and adequate means of livelihood.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: economic equality rests on Article 39, a Directive Principle, not on the Fundamental Duty in Article 51A. Statement 2 is incorrect: Article 39 is a Directive Principle of State Policy and is not enforceable by the courts. Statement 3 is correct: Article 39 directs the State to secure equal pay for equal work for men and women and adequate means of livelihood.
w: '1 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect, and leaves out statement 3, which is correct.
'2 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect, and leaves out statement 3, which is correct.
'1 and 3 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about fraternity:

1. Fraternity reflects emotional unity, mutual respect and a sense of belonging among citizens.
2. Fraternity cannot exist unless the dignity of every individual is protected and respected.
3. The unity and integrity of the Nation promotes national cohesion across religion, caste, region and language.
4. The Preamble declares that fraternity must assure the dignity of the Nation and the unity and integrity of the individual.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: fraternity reflects emotional unity, mutual respect and a sense of belonging among citizens. Statement 2 is correct: fraternity cannot exist unless the dignity of every individual is protected and respected. Statement 3 is correct: the unity and integrity of the Nation promotes national cohesion, overcoming communalism, regionalism, casteism and linguism. Statement 4 is incorrect: the Preamble assures the dignity of the individual and the unity and integrity of the Nation, not the reverse.
w: '1, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect, and leaves out statement 2, which is correct.
'1, 2 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect, and leaves out statement 3, which is correct.
'1 and 2 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Ambedkar's 'union of trinity':

1. Ambedkar held that liberty, equality and fraternity are not separate items but form a union of trinity.
2. According to Ambedkar, political democracy can last even when social democracy does not lie at its base.
3. In Ambedkar's passage, liberty and equality cannot be divorced from fraternity, just as they cannot be divorced from each other.
4. Social democracy in this sense is a way of life that recognises liberty, equality and fraternity.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Ambedkar held that liberty, equality and fraternity are not separate items but form a union of trinity. Statement 2 is incorrect: he said political democracy cannot last unless social democracy lies at the base. Statement 3 is correct. Statement 4 is correct: Social democracy in this sense is a way of life that recognises liberty, equality and fraternity.
w: '1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct:
'1 and 3 only' leaves out statement 4, which is correct:
'1, 2 and 4 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct:

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about amendments to the Preamble:

1. The 42nd Amendment inserted the words Socialist and Secular between Democratic and Republic.
2. The 1976 amendment of the Preamble has been held to be valid by the Supreme Court.
3. The word Sovereign was in the Preamble from the beginning and means India is internally and externally free.
4. The word Republic was added to the Preamble in 1976.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: the 42nd Amendment inserted Socialist and Secular between Sovereign and Democratic, not between Democratic and Republic. Statement 2 is correct: the 1976 amendment of the Preamble has been held valid by the Supreme Court, which dismissed petitions against it in 2024. Statement 3 is correct: 'Sovereign' was in the original Preamble and means India is internally and externally free. Statement 4 is incorrect: 'Republic' was in the original text; the 1976 additions were Socialist, Secular and Integrity.
w: '1 and 2 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect, and leaves out statement 3, which is correct.
'1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect.
'2, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Supreme Court and the Preamble:

1. In the Berubari Union case (1960) the Supreme Court held the Preamble to be an integral part of the Constitution.
2. In Kesavananda Bharati (1973) the Court held the Preamble to be a part of the Constitution, amendable under Article 368 provided its basic structure is not altered.
3. The Supreme Court's 1995 ruling in the LIC of India case again treated the Preamble as an integral part of the Constitution.
4. In Berubari the Court said the Preamble is a key to the minds of the makers, showing the general purpose behind the provisions, and can help interpret ambiguous articles.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: Berubari held that the Preamble is not part of the Constitution and not enforceable. Statement 2 is correct: In Kesavananda Bharati (1973) the Court held the Preamble to be a part of the Constitution, amendable under Article 368 provided its basic structure is not altered. Statement 3 is correct: The Supreme Court's 1995 ruling in the LIC of India case again treated the Preamble as an integral part of the Constitution. Statement 4 is correct: In Berubari the Court said the Preamble is a key to the minds of the makers, showing the general purpose behind the provisions, and can help interpret ambiguous articles.
w: '1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct:
'2 and 3 only' leaves out statement 4, which is correct:
'2 and 4 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct:

3. The words in question had been added during the Emergency, in 1976.

questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: they challenged the 42nd Amendment of 1976. Statement 2 is correct. Statement 3 is correct: The words in question had been added during the Emergency, in 1976.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about fraternity and the Preamble:

1. Fraternity means a sense of brotherhood, which the Constitution promotes through the system of single citizenship.
2. Article 1 describes India as a 'Federation of States' so as to make clear that the states cannot secede from the Union.
3. K.M. Munshi read the phrase 'dignity of the individual' as recognising that the personality of every individual is sacred, beyond material betterment and a democratic set-up.
4. The national integration at which the words 'unity and integrity of the Nation' aim has a territorial side as well as a psychological side.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: fraternity means a sense of brotherhood, promoted through the system of single citizenship. Statement 2 is incorrect: Article 1 calls India a 'Union of States', which makes clear that the states have no right to secede. Statement 3 is correct: K.M. Munshi read 'dignity of the individual' as recognising that the personality of every individual is sacred. Statement 4 is correct: national integration has both a territorial and a psychological dimension. So only three of the statements are correct.
w: 'Only two' undercounts: statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct.
'All four' overcounts: statement 2 is incorrect, since Article 1 says 'Union' of States.
'Only one' undercounts: statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the 42nd Amendment and the Preamble:

1. The 42nd Amendment inserted three words: Socialist, Secular and Republic.
2. To date the sole amendment to the Preamble is the 42nd Amendment of 1976.
3. The 42nd Amendment inserted 'Socialist' and 'Secular' into the Preamble.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: the three words were Socialist, Secular and Integrity. Statement 2 is correct: To date the sole amendment to the Preamble is the 42nd Amendment of 1976. Statement 3 is correct. So only two of the statements is correct.
w: 'Only one' miscounts: the correct statement(s) are 2, 3.
'None' miscounts: the correct statement(s) are 2, 3.
'All three' miscounts: the correct statement(s) are 2, 3.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Ambedkar's argument on liberty, equality and fraternity:

1. According to the argument, liberty without equality produces domination by the few.
2. According to the same argument, equality without liberty produces the supremacy of the few over the many.
3. Ambedkar regarded liberty, equality and fraternity as separate ideals that can be pursued one at a time.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct:(supremacy of the few over the many). Statement 2 is incorrect: equality without liberty would kill individual initiative; it is liberty without equality that gives supremacy of the few. Statement 3 is incorrect: he said they are not separate items but a union of trinity. So only one of the statements is correct.
w: 'None' miscounts: the correct statement(s) are 1.
'Only two' miscounts: the correct statement(s) are 1.
'All three' miscounts: the correct statement(s) are 1.

questions.q:
Match the word of the Preamble in List-I with its significance in List-II.

List-I
A. Sovereign
B. Socialist
C. Secular
D. Integrity

List-II
1. Part of the Preamble from the beginning; no external power can dictate India's government
2. Added in 1976; made explicit the socialist content that Directive Principles already carried
3. Added in 1976; the State has no official religion and treats all religions equally
4. Added in 1976 by changing 'Unity of the Nation'; stresses territorial and psychological unity
questions.e: (significance table): Sovereign is original; Socialist, Secular and Integrity came with the 42nd Amendment.
w: Socialist and Secular are interchanged: the word that made explicit the existing Directive Principles content is Socialist; no official religion goes with Secular.
Sovereign and Integrity are interchanged: Sovereign is original, Integrity was added in 1976.
Sovereign and Socialist are interchanged: Sovereign is not a 1976 addition.
